label: dam-probes-p20-p23
_why: ENGINE PROBES, the follow-up set (user, 2026-09-28: "If there is time and obvious open questions once these probes are done, go on with the next set of probes, designed for these questions"; "I think the bureaucracy cost is a sufficient gate by itself. The trick is to make it work for AI."). p19/p15/p16 (session 20260928_134653) showed the AI taking the survey DECISION itself when its spare bureaucracy (produced - used) exceeds the survey's cost: only the USA ever had that much spare in 1836-46 (the other majors ran within ~100 of their cap against survey costs of 600-1,500), and its surveys ran one after another, never two at once. Because that check serialises on its own, p15/p16's survey-count gates were never exercised and the same-day question was left open. This set LOOSENS the spare check so several surveys qualify at once. Arm: probe books (the class technologies granted to the ten majors at the start, construction cost x0.05), each = config/mod_config.probe-dam-p19.json with only dams.probe.decision_ai changed (p23 also drops the 2-month survey override, so surveys take their real 6-24 months).

p20.decision_ai: weight 10, no survey-count gate, headroom_mult 0 (any positive spare bureaucracy)

_questions.Q1: Does a country start two or more surveys on the SAME DAY (F168's 'every visible decision in one pass')?
_questions.Q2: How deep a bureaucracy deficit does it run into, and does the AI build government administration to cover it?

_predictions.Q1: unknown - the question; if yes, several surveys start the first day a major holds any spare
_predictions.Q2: a deficit of 1-3 surveys' cost, then administration built over a few years

p21.decision_ai: weight 10, no survey-count gate, headroom_mult 0.5 (spare above half the survey's cost)

_questions.Q1: Surveys per major over the decade against p19's (headroom_mult 1)?
_questions.Q2: Is the deficit it runs into bounded at about half a survey's cost?

_predictions.Q1: a few majors besides the USA survey, 1-3 each
_predictions.Q2: yes, usage at most ~half a survey above production

p22.decision_ai: weight 10, one-survey-at-a-time gate in POSSIBLE, headroom_mult 0

_questions.Q1: With p20's loose spare check, does a count gate in `possible` stop same-day multiple starts - i.e. is `possible` re-checked after each take within one AI pass?

_predictions.Q1: unknown - the question; compare against p20's same-day count

p23.decision_ai: weight 10, no survey-count gate, headroom_mult 0.5, REAL survey months, 20 years

_questions.Q1: With real survey lengths, how many surveys does a major run at once and how many does it complete in 20 years?
_questions.Q2: Does the bureaucracy stay near balance (the AI covering the survey cost by building administration), or drift into a sustained deficit?

_predictions.Q1: 1-2 at once for the USA and Britain, a handful completed

p18.note: RE-RUN of p18 from session 20260928_134653, whose build was rejected by preflight L1 (its seeded surveys used c:TAG ?= instead of an exists guard; fixed in emit_dams.mjs). Its questions are unchanged: see tools/testbed/schedules/dam_probe_p18_open_builders.json.

_cost: 3 runs x 1836 -> 1846.1 + 2 runs x 1836 -> 1856.1, about 90 minutes
_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30).
Probe builds: technologies granted, costs shrunk - no economic reading.
The survey_start log line reads bureaucracy BEFORE the survey's modifier is applied.
